utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. We are still on paragraph 4.1 of 5 the indictment. Looking still then at paragraph 4.1, there is the 9 further allegation of a beating of a number of Muslim males 10 seized and detained at Prijedor military barracks. One 11 observation we have to make about this is that it is outside 12 that time frame of 24th to 27th May that heads off this section 13 of paragraph 4.1 but, no doubt, those allegations fit elsewhere 14 within the framework of this case. Again, if I may make this observation, that there are 16 two witnesses alone who give evidence of beatings at Prijedor 17 barracks, Uzeir Besic and Sead Halvadzic. The allegation 18 concerning Uzeir Besic is on 3rd June 1992 and amounts after his 19 beating in the corridor of the barracks to a man he says was 20 Dusko Tadic giving him a kicking whilst he was on the ground 21 after his interrogation. Again, we have made observations about 22 how people are able to make these allegations and this kind of 23 sighting, and we emphasise that the Court will have to consider 24 carefully whether this is just one more allegation thrown into 25 the pot or happened. There does not seem to be in the context of this case 27 much other evidence that links Dusko Tadic with Prijedor 28 barracks. Our submission is that it is highly isolated and we would say something that the Court should treat with extreme caution, particularly when one considers the evidence of the second witness, Sead Halvadzic, who was there on 8th June 1992 having been taken captive. This was one of the identification witnesses who had not known Dusko Tadic before. His identification of the defendant using the photospread on, I believe, 14th June 1996, over four years later, a black and white photograph, having resided in a country where the newspaper that he claimed to have only looked at, [redacted] we know from the media expert, Thomas Deichmann, who gave evidence, had printed some 82 articles between February 1994 and October 1996 containing information about Dusko Tadic. Interestingly as well, within his evidence all his allegations concerning his own beating and indeed people he came across, if I can put it this way, refer to all the big names in Omarska -- Meakic and others. We submit to the Court that his evidence should be taken with extreme caution, particularly in view of some four years later using the photospread as a means of identification in circumstances when there had been a great deal of publicity about this case throughout the world. 23 JUDGE STEPHEN: Mr. Kay, what did you say, that he claimed to have only looked at [redacted] 25 MR. Perhaps it affects the subconscious of this kind of 11 witness to put it in his memory bank, so to speak, so that when 12 that photospread is laid before him there is something there 13 that triggers a recollection. One has to be wary of this, 14 particularly when a gap of four years has existed between what 15 amounts to a fairly brief confrontation to a process of 16 identification. Quite why people would express 20 themselves in that way and in those circumstances is slightly 21 odd to imagine; quite why the name should be used at all is 22 difficult to conceive. But there we are. He said he did not 23 know this man, and claimed an identification many years later 24 through what, we would say, is a flawed process by them. Moving from paragraph 4.1, because paragraph 12 which 26 is referred to within that section of the indictment exists as a 27 separate substantive count, and I will address the Court about 28 that at the end of the addresses relating to those substantive counts on the indictment. One considers other districts of the world and you think how many people have had karate lessons within particular areas, it seems to be very much a common feature of their society and what young men undertook, perhaps even as part of their JNA training. In those circumstances, to give it a degree of importance or identifying feature, it is by no means an exclusive hallmark that could be applied. If Dusko Tadic was the only karate exponent within the district, it would have far greater significance than it, in fact, does. 1 THE PRESIDING JUDGE: Mr. Kay, can you help me with that? He had seen Fikret Harambasic naked 23 and with a battered body climb into the canal where he and 24 witness G were and he had seen witness G bite off Fikret 25 Harambasic's testicle during a fairly considerable period of 26 time.
